question: in res.sendStatus, is res.status always called before res.send?
why: status(), type(), then send(): no branches.

question: in res.redirect, is res.status always called before this.end?
why: status(status) runs unconditionally; both end() calls (HEAD and body) come after it.

question: in res.redirect, is res.location always called before res.format?
why: this.location(address) is evaluated on the line before this.format({...}).

question: in res.redirect, is res.format always called before res.status?
why: format() then status(), straight-line.

question: in res.send, is res.status always called before this.end?
why: status(304) only runs when req.fresh; a normal response reaches end() without it.

question: in res.send, is res.header always called before this.end?
why: Every set() is inside a case or an if; send(undefined) with status 200 sets no header before end().

question: in res.json, is res.header always called before res.send?
why: set('Content-Type') only when no Content-Type is set yet.

question: in res.json, is res.get always called before res.send?
why: this.get('Content-Type') is the if condition, which always runs, before send().

question: in res.format, is res.vary always called before res.header?
why: vary('Accept') runs before the if (key) branch that calls set().

question: in res.format, is res.header always called before next?
why: With no matching type and no default, next(createError(406)) runs and set() never does.

question: in res.attachment, is res.type always called before res.header?
why: type() only when a filename is given; set('Content-Disposition') always runs.

question: in res.sendFile, is pathIsAbsolute always called before sendfile?
why: pathIsAbsolute is on the right of `!opts.root &&`: skipped when a root is given.

question: in res.sendFile, is encodeURI always called before sendfile?
why: encodeURI(path) is straight-line code before send() and sendfile().

question: in app.handle, is res.setHeader always called before this.router.handle?
why: X-Powered-By is only set when the setting is enabled.

question: in app.handle, is app.enabled always called before this.router.handle?
why: this.enabled('x-powered-by') is an if condition, so it always runs first.

question: in app.render, is app.enabled always called before tryRender?
why: enabled('view cache') only runs when options.cache was not given.

question: in app.listen, is http.createServer always called before once?
why: createServer is the first statement; once() comes later and only with a callback.

question: in res.clearCookie, is cookie.serialize always called before res.append?
why: clearCookie -> cookie(); inside it serialize() is an argument of append(), so it runs first.

question: in res.sendStatus, is res.status always called before this.end?
why: status() runs before send(), the only way to end().

question: in res.json, is res.get always called before this.end?
why: get() runs before send(), the only way to end().

question: in res.sendStatus, is res.header always called before this.end?
why: type('txt') always calls set('Content-Type') before send() reaches end().

question: in res.jsonp, is res.header always called before this.end?
why: jsonp(undefined) with Content-Type already set and no callback calls send(undefined), which reaches end() without set().

question: in res.download, is contentDisposition.create always called before sendfile?
why: The Content-Disposition header is built before sendFile(), which calls sendfile().

question: in res.render, is app.render always called before res.send?
why: send() only happens in the callback that app.render() is given, so app.render() is called first.

question: in app.init, is app.enable always called before app.set?
why: init -> defaultConfiguration, whose first call is enable('x-powered-by'), and enable calls set().

question: in app.defaultConfiguration, is exports.compileETag always called before exports.compileTrust?
why: set('etag') (-> compileETag) runs before set('trust proxy') (-> compileTrust); which case runs depends on the setting's name.

question: from every entry point, is res.status always called before this.end?
why: res.send can be called directly and reaches end() without status().

question: from every entry point, is app.init always called before app.defaultConfiguration?
why: defaultConfiguration is only called by init().

question: from every entry point, is mixin always called before app.init?
why: init() is only called by createApplication(), after its mixin() calls.

question: from every entry point, is res.vary always called before res.header?
why: res.json and others call set() without vary().

question: from every entry point, is contentDisposition.create always called before sendfile?
why: res.sendFile is public and reaches sendfile() without download()'s header.

question: from every entry point, is encodeURI always called before sendfile?
why: sendfile() is only called by res.sendFile, after encodeURI().

question: from every entry point, is View always called before tryRender?
why: With view caching on, app.render reuses a cached view and skips new View().

question: in res.status, is res.header always called before this.end?
why: res.status only checks the code and sets statusCode.

question: in res.location, is res.get always called before this.end?
why: location() -> set() -> setHeader(); nothing ends the response.
